title: Design and sourcing
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity.
opportunity: Design-time evidence — unified view of RAM, recycled-content rules, reuse/refill and forward-fee effects before formats are locked, so innovators can compare materials without compliance becoming anti-innovation. Trace: OPP-003/015/016; WOA cluster on modulated fees and evidenced design choices.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers proactively design out unrecyclable elements before waste exists. They use RAM, recycled-content, reuse/refill, forward-fee, and environmental impact evidence before design choices are locked, so compliance burden does not become a hindrance to packaging innovation. They can test whether smaller paper packaging, glass, compostable packaging, or reuse/refill routes will be rewarded or penalised before committing. Evidence: UN-056, UN-057, UN-058, UN-062, UN-064; E-110, E-111, E-112, E-114, E-118, E-119, E-121; Areas A, G, H, I.
successMeasure: Proportion of packaging assessed against RAM before launch; Proportion of design decisions using forward fee or scenario modelling; proportion of relevant plastic packaging with recycled-content evidence; reduced producer effort to obtain RAM and fee evidence; Fewer cases where lower-material, glass, or compostable options are avoided because the EPR classification or fee signal is unclear. Evidence: SPI-001, SPI-002, E-110, E-111, E-112, E-118, E-119, E-121.

title: Establish compliance strategy
envOutcomes: ENV-02 Increase circularity; ENV-03 Prevent waste crime where unclear responsibility weakens compliance coverage.
opportunity: Clarity pathways — proportional guidance and segmented support so organisations know obligation, route (producer vs scheme vs import), accountable roles, and whether EPR/DWT/RAM applies before deadlines bite, shrinking paid interpretation and mis-registration. Trace: OPP-001/002/005/007/030/032/033.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers, importers, distributors, and indirect supply-chain actors identify whether EPR, RAM, or DWT applies, choose the right direct or scheme route, and assign accountable people before deadlines; Policy and support teams simplify EPR policy into clearer decision paths and avoid assuming that a blunt large/small producer split explains actual burden or support need. Evidence: UN-037, UN-039, UN-040, UN-053, UN-054, UN-056, UN-063, UN-068, UN-094, UN-095; E-109, E-113, E-115, E-117; Areas B, G, H, J.
successMeasure: % correctly identifying obligation and route before registration; Time to determine obligation status and begin registration; reduced late, misrouted, or unsupported registrations; Reduced avoidable support queries from non-obligated supply-chain actors; Reduced need for paid advice or manual interpretation caused by policy complexity. Evidence: SPI-006, SPI-007, SPI-008, SPI-012, SPI-016, UN-037, UN-056, UN-063, UN-068, UN-094, E-109, E-117.

title: Produce goods
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity.
opportunity: Manufacturing fidelity — tooling and BOM data wired to taxonomy so production choices stay aligned with evidence submitted downstream — avoiding late BOM vs reporting drift. Trace: OPP-003/008/013.
ideas:
Tie works-order / SKU master data to canonical material IDs used in submissions;
Flag when a POM change shifts RAM tier or obligated tonnage before stock ships;
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers maintain component-level packaging records and classify household status, nation of sale, dual-use packaging, and responsibility boundaries consistently. Evidence: UN-055, UN-058, UN-065, UN-076; PP-055, PP-058, PP-065, PP-076.
successMeasure: % submissions classified correctly first time; Time and effort to gather supply-chain data; Reduced misclassification across household status, nation of sale, and dual-use packaging. Evidence: SPI-001, SPI-002, SPI-003, UN-055, UN-058, UN-065, UN-076.

title: Consumer communication and labelling
envOutcomes: ENV-02 Increase circularity, with evidence gap for direct consumer-stage impact.
opportunity: Trusted on-pack/disposal signalling where it changes sorting — consistent with RAM narratives UK/EU shifts without overwhelming SMEs with perpetual label churn (change-fatigue surfaced in evidence). Trace: OPP-001/030/032.
ideas: Embed material iconography + BIN routes that reconcile to the same taxonomy as reporting;
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers apply clear, consistent consumer disposal information where evidence shows labelling decisions affect downstream sorting, while monitoring changing UK/EU requirements. Evidence: UN-063 and PP-063 show supply-chain actors need RAM and legislation clarity to support customers; G1 captures change fatigue.

title: Distribute packaged goods into the UK market
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity; ENV-03 Prevent waste crime through better responsibility and flow data.
opportunity: Continuous placement data versus end-of-cycle reconstruction — capture nation-of-sale, HH/NHH, depth of supply chains, and SKU diversity as-it-happens to power proportional interventions. Trace: OPP-003/004/008/014/029.
ideas: Alerts when distribution pattern trips new evidence or registration obligations;
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers collect market-placement, packaging complexity, supply-chain depth, nation-of-sale, and household/non-household data continuously rather than reconstructing it at submission time, so policy and service support can be segmented by real operating complexity and policy rules can become more flexible, targeted, and easier to apply than a one-size-fits-all journey. This should reduce reliance on painful manual data collection, package weighing, and spreadsheet reconstruction. Evidence: UN-055, UN-065, UN-076; E-113, E-114, E-115, E-116; Areas B, C, D, H.
successMeasure: % records with complete nation-of-sale and household/non-household classification; completeness of packaging variety, registration profile, submission complexity, and supply-chain-depth data where needed for segmentation; Reduced rework caused by missing or ambiguous supply-chain data; Evidence that support routes and policy analysis use these richer segments rather than blunt large/small producer categories; Reduced delays to compliance software investment caused by unstable requirements or fragmented communications, including organisations waiting for EU packaging regulation clarity before investing in bespoke tooling. Evidence: SPI-001, SPI-002, SPI-003, E-113, E-115, E-116.

title: Register as a producer and report packaging data
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity; ENV-03 Prevent waste crime through cleaner compliance coverage.
opportunity: Submission ergonomics & provenance of record — validations that teach, delegated authority surfaced, duplicate-scheme clashes prevented, higher quality first-pass data powering fees and audits. Trace: OPP-004/008/012/013/014/034/035.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers and schemes submit accurate packaging data on time, resolve validation issues before rework repeats, and can see whether registration, delegated authority, contact details, and key submission steps are complete. Evidence: UN-040, UN-042, UN-048, UN-053, UN-055, UN-065, E-102, E-103, E-104, E-106; Areas B, C, D, J.
successMeasure: % accepted at point of entry without rework; time/cost per rejected submission; reduced validation loops and avoidable support contacts; % journeys with clear completion status; Reduction in duplicate or conflicting scheme submissions. Evidence: SPI-004, SPI-005, E-102, E-104, E-106.

title: Financial fulfilment (taxes, fees, and trading)
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity.
opportunity: Transparent multi-channel forecasting — reconcile PRNs/PERNs, modulated/disposal/PPT/refill streams so finance and packaging leads share one explainable ledger, narrowing volatility shocks and rogue interpretations. Trace: OPP-015/016/017/018.
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers understand disposal fees, weight-based pEPR effects, RAM impacts, PRNs/PERNs, PPT, reuse/refill, and offsetting well enough to forecast costs and make packaging decisions with compliance cost visible upstream; policy and charging logic are simplified enough to explain, forecast, and challenge; charging and support feel proportionate because they account for real packaging and submission complexity, not only producer size bands. Evidence: UN-043, UN-044, UN-045, UN-047, UN-057, UN-066, UN-071; E-109, E-113, E-115, E-117, E-118, E-119, E-120, E-121; Areas A, C, H, I, J.
successMeasure: % producers able to explain fee basis; reduced disputes or off-service workarounds about fee calculations; Improved confidence in PRN/PERN and disposal-fee calculations; % design decisions where likely fee consequences are visible before commitment; Reduced support or paid-advice demand created by unclear policy or charging rules. Evidence: UN-043, UN-044, UN-045, UN-047, UN-057, UN-066, E-109, E-117, E-118, E-119, E-121.

title: End-of-life management
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity; ENV-03 Prevent waste crime where evidence gaps weaken assurance.
opportunity: Operational circularity connectors — evidenced reuse/refill/closed-loop paths that sit alongside disposal costs, supporting culture shifts evidenced in qualitative research — while keeping regulators confident chains are intact. Trace: OPP-015/017/018/027/031/032.
ideas:
Pair end-of-life routes with evidenced outcomes (deposit, community reuse, takemeback schemes);
Telemetry from PRN brokerage back into packaging SKU cards for next-cycle planning;
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers keep auditable evidence, use closed-loop or reuse/refill routes where viable, and apply continuous improvement loops to adjust packaging, evidence collection, reporting, and fee exposure before the next cycle, rather than treating successful compliance as a reason to freeze existing packaging choices. Service and policy design should learn from contexts where reuse and recycling feel socially normal and rewarding, such as bottle-return rewards that can become pocket money for children, community take-and-leave schemes, baby-sling sharing, and pride in reused items from tip-shop or community reuse routes. Evidence: UN-043, UN-044, UN-056, UN-058, UN-062, UN-064, UN-070, UN-071; E-107, E-114, E-121; Areas A, G, I, J.
successMeasure: Completeness of auditable evidence records; Reduced manual evidence reconciliation; Fewer repeated classification or fee issues in subsequent cycles. Evidence: SPI-031, SPI-032, SPI-033, UN-043, UN-044, UN-070.

title: Auditing & continuous improvement
envOutcomes: ENV-01 Reduce waste; ENV-02 Increase circularity; ENV-03 Prevent waste crime.
opportunity: Institutional learning loop — policy evaluation questions answered by collected fields; amend history and fee reconciliation visible without spreadsheets, powering proportionate interventions and forensic accountability across cycles. Trace: OPP-010/014/026/027/028/031/034/035.
ideas:
Comparative cohort analytics for compliance teams versus benchmark peers;
Data minimisation dashboards: strip fields unsupported by articulated policy hypotheses;
desiredBehaviourChange: Producers and regulators use trusted historical data, audit trails, fee/evidence reconciliation, and product-design feedback to improve future packaging decisions and spot non-compliance earlier. Data is collected because it answers explicit questions about policy evaluation and international comparison, accountability for public spending and system improvement, and fair taxation or charging. Evidence: E-003, E-004, E-005, E-022, E-026, E-030, E-100, E-105, E-115; Areas D, F, I, J.
successMeasure: Completeness of auditable evidence records; reduced manual evidence reconciliation; Fewer repeated classification or fee issues in subsequent cycles; Year-on-year comparisons available without spreadsheet reconstruction; Audit trail sufficient to explain changes; evidence that collected fields are used for policy evaluation, accountability, fair charging, or are inferred from existing government sources where possible. Evidence: SPI-031, SPI-032, SPI-033, E-003, E-004, E-030, E-100, E-115.
